original_card.question: Is there a genuinely unsearched, explicitly bounded improvement to the selected packing?
methods: Search a named unclaimed canonical candidate domain with a reproducible partition.
Prove a stronger scoped relaxation or exact optimum for one named residual subproblem.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Check live PR overlap first, price both suppliers and distinguish a search best from an optimum. Report the word's packing cap from ceiling.ceiling() and the fraction of it realized; label packing gains as such.

first_step.inspect: Locate the selected packing source in the review and check live PRs for the same residual problem.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Define an unclaimed canonical domain and a favorable bound before starting a new search.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An actual paid-profile gain can improve the frontier up to the other supplier cap.
allowed_variations: One bounded residual packing instance or exact relaxation.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Rerunning an existing search with only a different seed as a separate mathematical contribution.

existing_checks.scope: Packing-independent ceiling for the selected paid profile under the one-unpaid-coordinate coverage and halving guard.
existing_checks.remaining: A changed word or model requires new pricing; a local packing search must name uncovered scope.

actual_scope: Is there a genuinely unsearched, explicitly bounded improvement to the selected packing?
bottleneck_link: A better owner packing changes the idle residual profile of the fixed complex supplier and therefore improves its exactly priced endpoint, while staying below the same word-level ceiling. The bit supplier, local word, coverage law, template, and outer guard remain fixed.
stop_rule: Keep the best exact-kappa map, then stop this bounded session after strict and independent replay and 24 subsequent evacuation/relocation/call/time-window neighbourhood rounds fail to improve exact kappa. This is a search stop, not an optimality criterion.
evidence: SEARCH.json and evidence/: an OR-Tools CP-SAT evacuation neighbourhood produced a strict-replayed candidate at exact kappa 0.001673618490895016, up 4.285169321e-9 (0.0002560428% relative) over the immediately preceding map. The independent seed67 audit, exact pricing of both suppliers, PR1069 sweep, and unchanged 11-stage strict replay pass with controls 69/12/6/15. ceiling.ceiling() gives a_hi=0.001690054109089 and implied kappa ceiling 0.001687202645325402; the candidate realizes 99.194871% of that ceiling. The exact packing certificate remains E<=908139.013 and at most 4,887 empty cap-48 bins (candidate: 4,880); it is not a kappa bound. No optimum is claimed. The live 2026-10-17 21:23 UTC overlap refresh returned 350 open PRs and 321 discussion records, with no matching open T16 owner-packing PR; nearest scoped results are recorded in SEARCH.json and evidence/OVERLAP.json.

open_questions.question: Can exact supplier costs drive a decomposed master problem with pricing cuts more effectively than a rounded separable moment objective?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Three bounded rounded-moment CP-SAT probes produced no strict kappa gain, and the accepted map has higher surrogate E than its predecessor despite higher exact kappa. The residual profile is coupled through the exact supplier pricing function, so a master/pricing loop may preserve more of the true objective structure.
open_questions.first_step: Use the pinned exact engines to price a bounded set of residual-profile moves, derive valid discrete marginal cuts for a small master problem, then reconstruct and strict-replay every proposed owner map.
open_questions.blocked_by: No exact or safely useful discrete cut description for the nonlinear aggregate pricing function has been derived; the three local moment probes are exploratory and do not establish a local optimum.

open_questions.question: Can the fixed-word kappa ceiling be tightened to a certificate on the remaining gap, or can a concrete packing approach it further?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The current candidate realizes 99.194871% of the word ceiling, but the ceiling is an endpoint relaxation rather than a packing optimum, and seven more empty cap-48 bins remain possible under the coarse packing certificate.
open_questions.first_step: Price the exact bound-attaining and near-bound idle profiles, then formulate a small residual-class CP-SAT model with exact post-pricing of its realized maps.
open_questions.blocked_by: The current E and empty-bin bounds do not imply a kappa bound or a realizable owner map.
